correctness.rationale: The substitution a=2b-c and character orthogonality give the exact sparse multiplication f_chi f_psi=N f_(-chi) when psi=-2chi, and zero otherwise. The Leibniz equation for that nonzero pair forces Df_(-chi) to lie in its own line: only one term from each Fourier expansion survives because doubling is bijective. The resulting relation lambda_(-chi)=lambda_chi+lambda_(-2chi), applied at chi and -chi, forces oddness on the doubles and hence everywhere; it then reduces to doubling the eigenvalue, with lambda_0=0. These equations also suffice on all zero products. The two possible orbit lengths and resonance conditions follow from whether inversion is half of a doubling cycle or exchanges two such cycles, giving dimension one or zero on each signed orbit. Characteristic zero and two are correctly excluded from resonance. Linear equation ranks are preserved by extension, and Galois descent pairs the appropriate Fourier labels. For primes ell congruent to 3 mod 8, the order of 2 has even order with odd half, by the quadratic-character test and ell-1 having 2-adic valuation one. Hence 2 to the half-order is -1 both modulo ell and over characteristic three. The two signs in the convolution Leibniz test are both negative by the quadratic character, giving -2c=c in characteristic three. The orders for 11 and 43 are 10 and 14 respectively. The reviewed checker only covers selected cyclic cases and was not executed.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Over a splitting field, partition the characters by the cyclic subgroup they generate. A nonzero product stays within its subgroup block, and cross-block multiplication is zero. Each basis vector of a block is a product of vectors in that block, so Leibniz forces every other block's component of its image to be zero. For a cyclic subgroup of order d, the block is isomorphic to the exact-order-d direct factor of the cyclic d algebra, taking characters to the corresponding units after choosing a generator; the singleton trivial block has zero derivations. The previously classified cyclic derivations restrict and extend by zero on that factor. Thus grouping old orbit contributions by the number of cyclic subgroups of each order gives the noncyclic formula, with no new resonance or operator type. The exhibited infinite family and its dimensions follow by the prior formula and the elementary order and Legendre-symbol calculations.
